# Dissipative Locality and Accuracy

This repository characterizes stationary approximation of pure quantum targets
when each Lindblad jump is confined to an allowed support and global coherent
control is unrestricted. The scientific account is organized by topic.

Canonical entrypoints:
- README.md: question, central error law, scientific routes, reproduction and scope.
- science/model.md: complete finite-dimensional model, existential localized
  representation condition, fidelity convention and optimization quantifiers.
- science/converse.md: leading stationary eigenvector, spectral population
  balance, local minimum eigenvalue bound, binary overlap argument, and the
  exact distance to pure states with a rank-deficient allowed marginal.
- science/construction.md: least-component truncation, one supported reset,
  projector-eigenbasis Jacobi Hamiltonian, uniqueness and global attraction.
- science/examples.md: structured targets and the positive/zero-marginal boundary.
- science/consequences.md: uniform marginals, finite-accuracy support requirements,
  Haar marginal concentration and its uniform support-family probability bound.
- science/resources.md: what is optimized, global Hamiltonian implementation,
  convergence limits, actual jump support and changes of physical model.
- references/RELATED_WORK.md: exact primary comparisons, inherited ingredients,
  source versions and limits of the literature comparison.
- references/references.bib: structured primary-source bibliography.
- learning/ANCHOR.md: the single educational anchor, Rivas–Huelga (2012), fixed
  arXiv:1104.5242v2; focused source routes, notation and the bridge to this result.
- learning/MILESTONES.md: exactly 30 project-defined understanding targets,
  connecting background/preliminaries to the narrative and scientific contribution.
- verification/README.md: actual reproducible checks and their scientific limits.
- verification/verify.py: finite construction and structured-state checks.
- verification/results.json: recorded numerical and exact-check output.

Reader routes:
- Scientific story: model, converse, construction, examples, consequences, resources.
- Study: learning/ANCHOR.md, then the two phases in learning/MILESTONES.md;
  follow their pointers to the authoritative science without requiring a full-book read.
- Proof inspection: begin with the exact model and then read the relevant full proof.
- Numerical reproduction: follow verification/README.md; separate finite checks
  from universal statements established analytically.
- Attribution: read RELATED_WORK.md before assigning originality to a mechanism.

Preserve these distinctions:
- mu includes zero eigenvalues of the full reduced-state matrix; it is not the
  smallest nonzero Schmidt weight.
- epsilon is 1-<psi|rho|psi>, not trace distance or one minus root fidelity.
- The mixed optimum is bounded between mu/2 and mu; the pure optimum equals mu.
- The all-stationary converse needs a nonscalar jump. Global attraction already
  excludes scalar-only or purely Hamiltonian dynamics on a nontrivial system.
- A generator is admissible if it has at least one representation with every
  jump supported on an allowed region. General channel mixing changes displayed
  supports without necessarily changing admissibility.
- The target need not be an eigenvector of the stationary density matrix.
- The Hamiltonian is arbitrary and global. The converse survives stronger
  restrictions, while the matching upper construction uses global freedom.
- The Jacobi basis must diagonalize the projector J-dagger J.
- The construction includes mu=0 and supports larger than their complements.
- A bounded Hamiltonian norm does not imply efficient specification, simulation
  or preparation. No general mixing-time law or optimal lower coefficient is proved.
- Local microscopic bath couplings need not yield locally supported effective jumps.
- Exact-state rank obstructions, spectral population balance, Hamiltonian-assisted
  attraction and random marginal concentration are inherited tools.
- Numerical checks and internal proof reviews do not constitute external peer review.
